From Andrew Craig,NORTHUMBERLAND

If like me, your +3 refuses to
produce an expanded Copy on the
Brother HR5 (Centronics), and
poking whatever number you like
at 23419 (DUMPLF) doesn't make a
blind bit of difference, then
here is the answer...

10 FORMAT LPRINT "U"
   (stops the Spectrum filtering
   out control codes to printer)

20 LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ 65;CHR$ 5
   (correct line pitch)

30 LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ 56;
   (neglect paper empty)

40 COPY EXP
   (or COPY EXP INVERSE)

This should give you perfect
expanded screen dumps to the end
of a piece of A4. I don't
understand why the manual tells
you to reduce the line pitch (at
the expense of quality) if your
printer produces a paper empty
error near the end of the page,
when you can simply instruct the
printer to ignore the paper
empty function. Weird.

Finally, I recently purchased
DATEL's Genius Mouse and Artist
2 (+3 version). The mouse is
great and Artist Two would be,
but for the fact that none of
the screen dump options work
with my Brother HR5 (parallel).
Can anyone help? I have had to
resort to amending the BASIC to


utilise the +3's existing dump
routines which is unsatisfactory
since the small dump doesn't
copy the bottom two lines of the
screen. I get the impression
that the conversion of Artist 2
to +3 format was a rushed job
since after calling some options
the Artcode becomes corrupted, I
suspect through sloppy RAM
paging. Am I right, or do I have
a defective copy?

P.S. I'm not sure if I told you
what types of setup I have in my
last letter. I have two setups:

 1) 48+, +D (New ROM & +2a SYS),
  Viglen 5 1/4" drive. 40/80T DS
 2) 128+3. I share a Brother HR5
  between the two.

P.P.S. A plug for women - My
wife uses the 48 setup as a word
processor/spreadsheet and admits
she doesn't know why she didn't
get into it before. Perhaps if
more women would only try using
a computer they would soon real-
ise how easy they are to use.


Thanks Andrew. No, ARTIST II has
always been notorious for its
print-out failures as well as
its other bugs. I long ago gave
up all attempts to print screens
from it. In addition, the HR5 is
not completely Epson-compatible.
If anyone else has managed to
hack the code to get dumps on an
HR5, please let us know.
                        - Brian

From Francis Davies, DORSET

Dear Ron,

Some time ago I was using some
disks on my +3 when, on CAT, I
was getting "Drive A, Track 1,
Sector 2, Missing Address Mark"
and on retry, "Data error". Also
"Drive A, Track 0, Sector 0, no
data" or "data error". This was
not on all disks at first but
over a few hours it had spread
to all disks.The only commercial
disk I possess (Robocop) would
not load on "loader" and the
instruction to load tape
appeared on the screen (i.e. the
drive had apparently not
detected the presence of a disk
in the drive).

I tried formatting a new, unused
blank disk but CAT only gave the
usual "data error". I therefore
assumed the problem lay in the
drive itself - not the disks.

Then I received your letter
saying"disks being left too near
the television may corrupt the
magnetic data".YES!-ALL my disks
lived in a plastic box VERY near
the TV! My heart sank - so I had
lost the lot! I then tried the
March copy of OUTLET you sent me
and... IT LOADED PERFECTLY! So,
the disk drive must be o.k. I
was so relieved I then moved the
TV to the far left and the +3 to
the far right of the shelf below
(so TV and drive were further
away from each other) and tried
loading my own disks...

THEY ALL LOADED PERFECTLY! I had
lost NONE of them! At first I
could not believe it but I'm
sure you can picture my relief
and pleasure and my saying over
and over "Thank you, Ron!".

Finally, you say, "...items may
be extracted for your own use".
As a beginner to the computer
world I should be grateful if
you would explain how to do
this. For example, in OUTLET 30,
the TRI TRI text says " perhaps
you could check my BASIC". How
can I see the BASIC used?

              - Francis Davies

To Francis Davies from Brian

Good to hear the magnetic inter-
ference did no permanent damage!

OUTLET programs can be examined
by using BREAK and LIST but in
128K mode it is best to enter
BASIC and MERGE a program before
using LIST because high memory
is paged out so new character
sets are rendered "invisible".

Alternatively, BREAK then POKE
23607,60(but you cannot see what
you are typing!). However, code
we use to suppress auto loading
of the DISK file when BREAK and
ENTER is used may crash on BREAK
on the latest +3 and +2A so
MERGE is safest.

From Steve Hill, KENT


Dear Brian & Ron,

I have been receiving Outlet for
about 9 months and would like to
congratulate you on its consist-
ently high standard. Here, I
refer not only to the content
but also to its presentation and
good, clear English.

My set-up comprises a 48K
Spectrum with a +D, DSDD 3.5"
drive and a "Two Face", the last
enabling me to run my old
Alphacom 32 printer. The whole
system is contained and perm-
anently wired in a strong case
about 27" x 13".

The hardware is mounted on a
chipboard base with all wiring
below and out of sight. Beneath
that is a layer of cushioning
foam.The detachable lid contains
more foam.

Power input is via a "Euro-plug"
and there is a 3-pin mains
outlet socket to accomodate the
TV monitor.


I found the system to be very
prone to crashing and this was
overcome by...

(i) bolting down the computer,
Two Face and +D - using homemade
brackets affixed with Loctite
'Multibond' 2-part adhesive


(ii) inserting a mains filter.

(iii) obviating the need for
ribbon extensions by replacing
the original short multicore
cable of the printer.

I can now laugh at the interfer-
ence "spikes" from such units as
the washing machine,deep freezer
and other thermostats and the
system is proof against vibrat-
ion from keyboard use.

Compatibility between computer/
+D and Alphacom is not 100% even
with Two Face, however.Just hav-
ing the printer plugged in may
cause a crash if blocks of code
are called by programs. Perhaps
that's why MGT no longer advert-
ise the Two Face?

If you have any ideas as to a
cure they would be most welcome.
There are no problems with BASIC
programs and TW2.

By the way, have you heard of a
supplier of paper for the
Alphacom 32? I am nearly out of
stock and have lost the last
address!


Many thanks for all the inform-
ation about SAM. The various
problems are reminiscent of the
Spectrum's and QL's early affl-
ictions so perhaps it will EVEN-
TUALLY be a worthy successor! If
MGT are not careful, they will
miss the market which would be a
shame.

Personally, I would not buy
until reasonably satisfied that
all bugs have been removed -
customers should not be expected
to undertake the company's
research and development.

As a matter of interest, the +D
has the command FORMAT D1 TO D2
with a like ridiculous purpose
to that which you encountered;
the handbook has the bold
warning BE CAREFUL NOT TO FORMAT
THE WRONG DISC!! That said, I
find the +D syntax and operation
to be excellent overall.

                  - Steve Hill

To Steve Hill fom Brian



The Alphacom has a fault which
causes trouble with many other
peripherals just, as you say, by
being connected.It seems strange
the TWO FACE doesn't isolate it
totally.


You can get a pack of 5 thermal
paper rolls for the Alphacom
from MICROSNIPS, 37 Seaview Rd.,
Wallasey, Merseyside L45 4QN for
`11.95 inc. postage.

                     - Brian

From L.M. McKechnie, YORKS

Dear Sirs,

I recently received OUTLET 32
and, whilst it is obviously a
well-composed and selected group
of articles,it lacks the ability
to cater for particular comput-
ers such as the +3 due obviously
to lack of capacity on the discs
etc. A compilation of articles
selected from early OUTLETs and
relevant to the +3 would
certainly interest me if one was
available![to add to EXTRA 1]

I was less than happy with the
32-col. print-out on my Seikosha
SL80AI set-up.This makes retent-
ion of hard copy very difficult.

Just one further point which
requires help is the ability to
transfer articles from the
current OUTLET disc to another
disc in order to allow me to
retain articles of interest in a
compact form and dispose of the
ones not required.

        Yours sincerely,

          L. McKechnie

To. Mr. L. McKechnie from Brian

We certainly intend to produce
more EXTRA compilations of early
OUTLET material but it's the old
enemy TIME that's delaying us.

Meanwhile, as you may have read
in this month's editorial, we're
expanding OUTLET by putting some
more material on the back of the
+3 disc and we may increase the
FORMAT even further to 203K per
side! Remember, OUTLET is YOUR
magazine so +3 users are welcome
to send in +3-specific programs,
articles and info. I think we've
had some marvellous +3-specific
programs in OUTLET already,
including SUPERMAT, CATSCAN and
this month's CATLOADER!

Speaking of which, and in answer
to your final query, the EASIEST
way to transfer OUTLET programs
to other +3 discs is now to use
CATLOADER!You could also use the
COPY command described on P.159
of the +3 manual. Alternatively,
BREAK or MERGE (as described in
my reply to Francis Davies) then
SAVE with RUN 9972 on +3; 9982
on M/Drive,Disciple/+D and Opus;
9983 for tape and 9985 for the
Sam Coupe. All our programs are
open for examination and are
unprotected AND we are glad to
help those with specific copying
problems - Just write!

As for our print-outs,next month
we have Mike Haine's 3 cols x 32
chars, we're calling "TABLOID".
It's excellent!        - Brian

From Frank Harrop, BRIGHTON


Dear Ron,

I thought I would give you an
update on the progress (or lack
of it!) on the Sam Coupe. As you
know mine, like yours, was
returned to Swansea for checking
and was returned simply "no
faults found" and of course the
problem of the tape loading
still remains, as well as the
lack of programs, apart from
games, that will transfer.

They did send me a cassette with
the latest issue 3 of the
utility - and as you may well
guess IT WOULD NOT LOAD even

though the other side of the
cassette with an earlier utility
did! It was returned last Satur-
day, the same day as received,
with a note "Please try again".

In January I wrote with a tape
containing the program "RADCALC"
both for the Spectrum and as
converted for the Sam, pointing
out that although it is all in
BASIC, when it is converted by
"btrans" it just refuses to work

corrupted.

You too may have received the
booklet on the eventual issue of

going to be a long time before
the machine becomes one we're
going to shout about using!

Thanks for all the interesting
information in Outlet 31 and do
keep it up - your efforts are
much appreciated.

           Sincerely,

          Frank Harrop

To Frank Harrop from Brian
     I converted the copy of
RADCALC you sent me to SAM using
"btrans" as you did" and found,
like you that it wouldn't work.
I then loaded ROMFIX (in last
month's and this month's issue
of OUTLET on SAM). This seemed
to cure the problem so I would
expect you will find it works
o.k. when the new SAM ROM is
issued (if you are not yet ready
to order the SAM version of
OUTLET to get ROMFIX). The
problem seems to be that VAL and
INPUT are not handled correctly
by the present ROM.
     I'd like to publish RADCALC
in OUTLET.Can you get permission
from the author or is it public
domain (FREEWARE)?    - Brian

From J.R. Cleveland, LONDON NW3

I've been subscribing to the +3
edition of "Outlet" for a few
months now and would like to say
how delighted I am with its
excellent standard of content
and presentation. Like many of
your other subscribers I am a
refugee from the sub-puerile
comic-strip Spectrum magazines.

The navigation system is most
impressive and the only improve-
ment (?) I could wish for - and
I'm not the first to suggest
this - is joystick control. The
benefit would be the pleasure of
enjoying Outlet"while decadently
laid back in one's armchair
instead of hunched up over the
keyboard.

Among the programs I have found
most useful are MINICHARSW in
Issue 23 and ROUTE 48 in No. 31.

I do have CP/M though I don't
use it very much. Mallard BASIC
makes a meal of things which are
so simple in Spectrum BASIC(e.g.
CLS), and it lacks graphics and
a screen-dump command (is there
really no way round this?).Also,
although it is several times
faster than Spectrum BASIC, if
you compile the latter with
HiSoft BASIC, then Mallard limps
home a poor second.

I've recently acquired a Star
LC10 colour printer, and the
first thing I found was that it
won't respond to the +3 without

POKE 23354,62 and POKE 23355,16.
(I believe this is also the case
with the Citizen 120D). What's
even odder is that these POKEs
must be followed by a STOP
command before printing from
some programs such as WORDMASTER
and OUTDEX is possible - a real
nuisance because it complicates
the loading procedure. Any ideas
what's going on?


I've also had problems with the
"LC10DRAW" program in "Outlet"
no. 30, despite having prefaced
it with the above-mentioned
POKEs and a FORMAT LPRINT "U"and
having successfully converted
the SAVE and LOAD commands to +3
syntax.

The difficulty comes when I try
to send anything to the printer,
having set the latter online and
with dipswitch 2-1 OFF as
instructed.The program then says
the printer is online, and stops
with "Nonsense in BASIC", appar-
ently caused by the POKE @VAL"6"
command which occurs several
times in the program and per-
plexes me as much as it does the
+3 editor - I think it's the "@"
which causes the problem.

The editorial in Outlet Extra 1
refers to a special +3 version
of UNITRANS+. But it would seem
that what I have on my 3" disc
is the microdrive version. If I
select the "manual" option,I get
a message at the foot of the


screen like SAVE * "m";1;"name"
LINE 1 which the +3 editor won't
accept. If I then delete the *
"m";1; and hit ENTER, I get a
system reset.

I enclose a sample printout made
with OUTPRINT. The problems
speak for themselves.

Let me conclude with some +3
conundrums...

1.Is it possible to do a NEW
without being thrown back to the
LOADER menu?

2.When "disk" is loaded directly
from the LOADER menu and during
RUNning gives rise to an error
message, any keypress causes the


LOADER menu to reappear and if
ENTER is accidently touched, the
program reloads from scratch. Is
there any way of gaining access
to the BASIC editor when such an
error occurs?

3.Lastly,is it possible to enter
SCREEN mode (i.e. the "lower"
screen) by means of an instruct-
ion within a program line?

         Yours sincerely

          J.R.CLEVELAND.

To Mr. J.R. Cleveland from Brian



After Charlie Kingwell's letter
in OUTLET 31 describing how he
paged through OUTLET on his back
and now your "cumfy armchair"
idea I'm getting the impression
our readership is so laid back
it's a wonder they switch on. So
we begin next month with cursor
control in text mode. Future
issues may use speech control
but someone may suffer a sore
throat so work has begun on an
alpha-wave detector that will
respond to thought. Ultimately,
each issue will come with a
lovely assistant who will turn
the pages for you!

Seriously, joysticks are out as
there are different standards.
Kempston crashes those without
it so a special routine would be
needed to detect it.The Sinclair
type uses the equivalent of some
number keys which are already in
use for pageing. Can anyone with
a Sinclair joystick confirm
this?

I can't help with CP/M but could
the HURRYDUMP (OUTLET 9) code be
used to dump text off-screen? If
a normal +3 code file can be
loaded or the file converted to
CP/M format and loaded then it
may work. I would expect there's
a public domain screen dump.Does
anyone know?

I see two possible approaches to
the +3 printer bug. One is to
disassemble the routine at 23354
to see exactly what it does with
the two POKEs and if it may be
achieved with some separate code
that doesn't need the program to
STOP. Another is to use an "ON
ERROR GO TO" piece of code that
will jump to another line of
BASIC if a STOP occurs. It seems
to me that in either case, the
code and/or POKEs might be
ideally placed in something like
CATLOADER so you would just need
to load whatever program you
want to use with CATLOADER and
it would be ready to print. I've
made a note to have a look at
the problem unless someone else
beats me to it...

The "POKE @ 6"'s in LC10 DRAW
are Disciple/+D printer commands
and should be replaced thus...

           POKE @ 6,1
           ----------
    +3        FORMAT LPRINT "U"

  OPUS OR
  M/DRIVE     OPEN #3;"B"
  OR SAM

 KEMPSTON E   COPY :REM CHR$ 0
              (may need separate
              line called by a
              GO SUB)

For POKE @6,0 replace above with
"E" for +3,"T" for Opus/M/drive,
"P" for SAM and CHR$ 1 for the
Kempston E.

I tried again to get UNITRANS +
to work on a +3. I thought I
managed to get a quick test
operating once although it was
important to be in"two-lines-at-
the-bottom-of-the- screen-edit-
mode" (there must be a better
name for it!). However, after
spending hours converting the
whole thing so the syntax was
correct I found, like you, that
it reset at the end. I'm almost
sure it did work once so I may
look at the problem again with a
fresh mind another day.

Mike Haine has re-written the
OUTPRINT code and it will appear
each month as an option in text
mode under the name "TABLOID"
starting next month.

It should be possible to write
some code to achieve NEW without
returning to the loader menu but
it would be more effort to load
the code than to return from the
menu.


I don't think there is any easy
way but would be delighted if
anyone knows differently as it
annoys me too!


You can SAVE a totally empty
BASIC program,that is,with NO
LINES AT ALL using SAVE"X".Then,
in normal programs, instead of
NEW, use LOAD"X" to clear out
BASIC.

The "feature" that re-loads
"DISK" if you press ENTER after
an error can be avoided in two
ways...

Firstly, DON'T PRESS ENTER! I
tend to press the down cursor to
cause the loader menu to show
and then again to select +3
BASIC and then ENTER.

The other way is to MERGE any
OUTLET"DISK" loader file, delete
all lines except 1001 and reSAVE
it. Then MERGE it in your own
programs or in a "DISK" loader
such as CATLOADER.You need a GO
SUB 1001 in the program.However,
Brian Gaff tells me this seems
to crash on later versions of
the +3 and +2A so try it first.

I have been trying to solve your
final query to switch to lower-
screen mode from within a
program to use in the +3 version
of UNITRANS+ but failed. Instead
of switching "screen" in the
loader menu you can press EXTEND
MODE then SYMBOL + 8 together
(another Brian Gaff tip!). This
works both ways. I reasoned that
SHIFTED-EXTENDED MODE 8 is POINT
on the original Spectrum (try it
in INPUT A$) and the code for
POINT is 169 so I had hoped if I
could enter 169 then 13 (ENTER)
into the ROM editor routine it
would switch "screen". However,
it didn't work although I did
discover methods of calling
BASIC commands from machine code
which may form the basis of a
future OUTLET utility!   -Brian

From David Wornham, WORCS.
  I am progressing well with the
SAM conversion of FLEXIPAGE,
hence the inclusion in OUTBOARD.
Any order received before it's
ready will receive a letter and
the cheque will not be paid in
before dispatch.

  I seem to have better luck
than you with MGT's service. I
received their updated DOS disk
on 16th March which includes a
couple of machine code "fixers".
This overcomes the SAVE problem
in MODE 1 but has yet to
overcome the problem of a SAVE
LINE command within a program
which SAVEs O.K. but stops with
an error message and the SAVE
DATA A$() with a program which

saves the PROGRAM AND DATA
whilst the direct command saves
correctly. However, MGT do say
the disk is a temporary measure
pending a replacement ROM.

MGT state,correctly,the external
drive/printer interface needs
the disk jumper REMOVED if two
internal drives are fitted.Their
new instructions include this.
They also state the DUMP command
is NOT IMPLEMENTED owing to lack
of space in the ROM. Although
they say use FLASH,I have yet to
get this to DUMP and it cannot
be included with FLEXIPAGE so I
shall write and urge them to
include it in the ROM update. In
the meantime, a SAM DUMP routine
would be a useful item in OUTLET
- please.       - David Wornham

To David Wornham from Brian


Thanks David. After receiving
your letter I decided to convert
our own high-res dump but I have
STILL not received the technical
manual I ordered from MGT so
cannot do any further work on
that for the time being.

I then sat down to attempt to
develop some BASIC screen dumps
and came up with TEEDEE & GEEDEE
in this month's issue(SAM ONLY).
Both are BASIC procedures with
high line numbers which can
easily be MERGEd in a program
with MERGE "TD" or "GD" and both
TD and GD are PD!! i.e. FREEWARE
so can be used in your programs.

The bad news is GD, the graphics
dump, is very slow and in modes
3 or 4 assumes palette colours 0
to 2 and 8 to 11 will be dark
and prints them as black and all
other colours come out white so
some screens do not print-out
perfectly. It is really intended
to be a temporary stopgap but
does include a nice method of
reducing streaking.

TD, the text dump is fast and
useful but uses the SCREEN$(X,Y)
function which seems to fail in
Mode 3 intermittently.

In FLASH,"DRAFT"and"FINAL"do not
work at all and probably try to
use the non-working ROM routine.
The other dump options are o.k.
                      - Brian

From Andrew Craig,NORTHUMBERLAND

If like me, your +3 refuses to produce an expanded Copy on the Brother HR5 (Centronics), and poking whatever number you like at 23419 (DUMPLF) doesn't make a blind bit of difference, then here is the answer...

10 FORMAT LPRINT "U" (stops the Spectrum filtering out control codes to printer)

20 LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ 65;CHR$ 5 (correct line pitch)

30 LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ 56; (neglect paper empty)

40 COPY EXP (or COPY EXP INVERSE)

This should give you perfect expanded screen dumps to the end of a piece of A4. I don't understand why the manual tells you to reduce the line pitch (at the expense of quality) if your printer produces a paper empty error near the end of the page, when you can simply instruct the printer to ignore the paper empty function. Weird.

Finally, I recently purchased DATEL's Genius Mouse and Artist 2 (+3 version). The mouse is great and Artist Two would be, but for the fact that none of the screen dump options work with my Brother HR5 (parallel). Can anyone help? I have had to resort to amending the BASIC to

utilise the +3's existing dump routines which is unsatisfactory since the small dump doesn't copy the bottom two lines of the screen. I get the impression that the conversion of Artist 2 to +3 format was a rushed job since after calling some options the Artcode becomes corrupted, I suspect through sloppy RAM paging. Am I right, or do I have a defective copy?

P.S. I'm not sure if I told you what types of setup I have in my last letter. I have two setups:

1) 48+, +D (New ROM & +2a SYS), Viglen 5 1/4" drive. 40/80T DS 2) 128+3. I share a Brother HR5 between the two.

P.P.S. A plug for women - My wife uses the 48 setup as a word processor/spreadsheet and admits she doesn't know why she didn't get into it before. Perhaps if more women would only try using a computer they would soon real- ise how easy they are to use.

Thanks Andrew. No, ARTIST II has always been notorious for its print-out failures as well as its other bugs. I long ago gave up all attempts to print screens from it. In addition, the HR5 is not completely Epson-compatible. If anyone else has managed to hack the code to get dumps on an HR5, please let us know.

From Francis Davies, DORSET

Dear Ron,

Some time ago I was using some disks on my +3 when, on CAT, I was getting "Drive A, Track 1, Sector 2, Missing Address Mark" and on retry, "Data error". Also "Drive A, Track 0, Sector 0, no data" or "data error". This was not on all disks at first but over a few hours it had spread to all disks.The only commercial disk I possess (Robocop) would not load on "loader" and the instruction to load tape appeared on the screen (i.e. the drive had apparently not detected the presence of a disk in the drive).

I tried formatting a new, unused blank disk but CAT only gave the usual "data error". I therefore assumed the problem lay in the drive itself - not the disks.

Then I received your letter saying"disks being left too near the television may corrupt the magnetic data".YES!-ALL my disks lived in a plastic box VERY near the TV! My heart sank - so I had lost the lot! I then tried the March copy of OUTLET you sent me and... IT LOADED PERFECTLY! So, the disk drive must be o.k. I was so relieved I then moved the TV to the far left and the +3 to the far right of the shelf below (so TV and drive were further away from each other) and tried loading my own disks...

THEY ALL LOADED PERFECTLY! I had lost NONE of them! At first I could not believe it but I'm sure you can picture my relief and pleasure and my saying over and over "Thank you, Ron!".

Finally, you say, "...items may be extracted for your own use". As a beginner to the computer world I should be grateful if you would explain how to do this. For example, in OUTLET 30, the TRI TRI text says " perhaps you could check my BASIC". How can I see the BASIC used?

- Francis Davies

To Francis Davies from Brian

Good to hear the magnetic inter- ference did no permanent damage!

OUTLET programs can be examined by using BREAK and LIST but in 128K mode it is best to enter BASIC and MERGE a program before using LIST because high memory is paged out so new character sets are rendered "invisible".

Alternatively, BREAK then POKE 23607,60(but you cannot see what you are typing!). However, code we use to suppress auto loading of the DISK file when BREAK and ENTER is used may crash on BREAK on the latest +3 and +2A so MERGE is safest.

From Steve Hill, KENT

Dear Brian & Ron,

I have been receiving Outlet for about 9 months and would like to congratulate you on its consist- ently high standard. Here, I refer not only to the content but also to its presentation and good, clear English.

My set-up comprises a 48K Spectrum with a +D, DSDD 3.5" drive and a "Two Face", the last enabling me to run my old Alphacom 32 printer. The whole system is contained and perm- anently wired in a strong case about 27" x 13".

The hardware is mounted on a chipboard base with all wiring below and out of sight. Beneath that is a layer of cushioning foam.The detachable lid contains more foam.

Power input is via a "Euro-plug" and there is a 3-pin mains outlet socket to accomodate the TV monitor.

I found the system to be very prone to crashing and this was overcome by...

(i) bolting down the computer, Two Face and +D - using homemade brackets affixed with Loctite 'Multibond' 2-part adhesive

(ii) inserting a mains filter.

(iii) obviating the need for ribbon extensions by replacing the original short multicore cable of the printer.

I can now laugh at the interfer- ence "spikes" from such units as the washing machine,deep freezer and other thermostats and the system is proof against vibrat- ion from keyboard use.

Compatibility between computer/ +D and Alphacom is not 100% even with Two Face, however.Just hav- ing the printer plugged in may cause a crash if blocks of code are called by programs. Perhaps that's why MGT no longer advert- ise the Two Face?

If you have any ideas as to a cure they would be most welcome. There are no problems with BASIC programs and TW2.

By the way, have you heard of a supplier of paper for the Alphacom 32? I am nearly out of stock and have lost the last address!

Many thanks for all the inform- ation about SAM. The various problems are reminiscent of the Spectrum's and QL's early affl- ictions so perhaps it will EVEN- TUALLY be a worthy successor! If MGT are not careful, they will miss the market which would be a shame.

Personally, I would not buy until reasonably satisfied that all bugs have been removed - customers should not be expected to undertake the company's research and development.

As a matter of interest, the +D has the command FORMAT D1 TO D2 with a like ridiculous purpose to that which you encountered; the handbook has the bold warning BE CAREFUL NOT TO FORMAT THE WRONG DISC!! That said, I find the +D syntax and operation to be excellent overall.

- Steve Hill

To Steve Hill fom Brian

The Alphacom has a fault which causes trouble with many other peripherals just, as you say, by being connected.It seems strange the TWO FACE doesn't isolate it totally.

You can get a pack of 5 thermal paper rolls for the Alphacom from MICROSNIPS, 37 Seaview Rd., Wallasey, Merseyside L45 4QN for `11.95 inc. postage.

- Brian

From L.M. McKechnie, YORKS

Dear Sirs,

I recently received OUTLET 32 and, whilst it is obviously a well-composed and selected group of articles,it lacks the ability to cater for particular comput- ers such as the +3 due obviously to lack of capacity on the discs etc. A compilation of articles selected from early OUTLETs and relevant to the +3 would certainly interest me if one was available![to add to EXTRA 1]

I was less than happy with the 32-col. print-out on my Seikosha SL80AI set-up.This makes retent- ion of hard copy very difficult.

Just one further point which requires help is the ability to transfer articles from the current OUTLET disc to another disc in order to allow me to retain articles of interest in a compact form and dispose of the ones not required.

Yours sincerely,

L. McKechnie

To. Mr. L. McKechnie from Brian

We certainly intend to produce more EXTRA compilations of early OUTLET material but it's the old enemy TIME that's delaying us.

Meanwhile, as you may have read in this month's editorial, we're expanding OUTLET by putting some more material on the back of the +3 disc and we may increase the FORMAT even further to 203K per side! Remember, OUTLET is YOUR magazine so +3 users are welcome to send in +3-specific programs, articles and info. I think we've had some marvellous +3-specific programs in OUTLET already, including SUPERMAT, CATSCAN and this month's CATLOADER!

Speaking of which, and in answer to your final query, the EASIEST way to transfer OUTLET programs to other +3 discs is now to use CATLOADER!You could also use the COPY command described on P.159 of the +3 manual. Alternatively, BREAK or MERGE (as described in my reply to Francis Davies) then SAVE with RUN 9972 on +3; 9982 on M/Drive,Disciple/+D and Opus; 9983 for tape and 9985 for the Sam Coupe. All our programs are open for examination and are unprotected AND we are glad to help those with specific copying problems - Just write!

As for our print-outs,next month we have Mike Haine's 3 cols x 32 chars, we're calling "TABLOID". It's excellent!        - Brian

From Frank Harrop, BRIGHTON

Dear Ron,

I thought I would give you an update on the progress (or lack of it!) on the Sam Coupe. As you know mine, like yours, was returned to Swansea for checking and was returned simply "no faults found" and of course the problem of the tape loading still remains, as well as the lack of programs, apart from games, that will transfer.

They did send me a cassette with the latest issue 3 of the utility - and as you may well guess IT WOULD NOT LOAD even

though the other side of the cassette with an earlier utility did! It was returned last Satur- day, the same day as received, with a note "Please try again".

In January I wrote with a tape containing the program "RADCALC" both for the Spectrum and as converted for the Sam, pointing out that although it is all in BASIC, when it is converted by "btrans" it just refuses to work - need I add that I have yet to hear from them on that.

I've received a disc with V. 1.3 of the DOS, as I had pointed out that with V. 1.1 any new disc to which DOS was transferred became corrupted.

You too may have received the booklet on the eventual issue of the upgrade pack. With the long list of bugs and faults,it is going to be a long time before the machine becomes one we're going to shout about using!

Thanks for all the interesting information in Outlet 31 and do keep it up - your efforts are much appreciated.

Sincerely,

Frank Harrop

To Frank Harrop from Brian I converted the copy of RADCALC you sent me to SAM using "btrans" as you did" and found, like you that it wouldn't work. I then loaded ROMFIX (in last month's and this month's issue of OUTLET on SAM). This seemed to cure the problem so I would expect you will find it works o.k. when the new SAM ROM is issued (if you are not yet ready to order the SAM version of OUTLET to get ROMFIX). The problem seems to be that VAL and INPUT are not handled correctly by the present ROM. I'd like to publish RADCALC in OUTLET.Can you get permission from the author or is it public domain (FREEWARE)?    - Brian

From Chris Powell

Dear Ron and Brian,

I'm kicking myself for not hav- ing sampled OUTLET before now! It's great to know there still are Spectrum owners out there not totally obsessed with games.

I use a +3 and Star LC10 for all manner of business operations though I have had a few problems with the LC10's compatibility. A printout from Master-file +3 still eludes me as the printer locks up when asked to perform a task. Have you any thoughts on how I might resolve the problem? Also, do you know if a ROM dissassembly exists for the +3?

To Chris Powell from Brian

You could try POKE 23354,62 : POKE 23355,16 as direct commands in BASIC before loading MASTER- FILE. The following letter from J.R. Cleveland also refers to this.

Regrettably, I'm fairly certain there's no published disassembly of the +3 ROM.

- Brian

From J.R. Cleveland, LONDON NW3

I've been subscribing to the +3 edition of "Outlet" for a few months now and would like to say how delighted I am with its excellent standard of content and presentation. Like many of your other subscribers I am a refugee from the sub-puerile comic-strip Spectrum magazines.

The navigation system is most impressive and the only improve- ment (?) I could wish for - and I'm not the first to suggest this - is joystick control. The benefit would be the pleasure of enjoying Outlet"while decadently laid back in one's armchair instead of hunched up over the keyboard.

Among the programs I have found most useful are MINICHARSW in Issue 23 and ROUTE 48 in No. 31.

I do have CP/M though I don't use it very much. Mallard BASIC makes a meal of things which are so simple in Spectrum BASIC(e.g. CLS), and it lacks graphics and a screen-dump command (is there really no way round this?).Also, although it is several times faster than Spectrum BASIC, if you compile the latter with HiSoft BASIC, then Mallard limps home a poor second.

I've recently acquired a Star LC10 colour printer, and the first thing I found was that it won't respond to the +3 without

POKE 23354,62 and POKE 23355,16. (I believe this is also the case with the Citizen 120D). What's even odder is that these POKEs must be followed by a STOP command before printing from some programs such as WORDMASTER and OUTDEX is possible - a real nuisance because it complicates the loading procedure. Any ideas what's going on?

I've also had problems with the "LC10DRAW" program in "Outlet" no. 30, despite having prefaced it with the above-mentioned POKEs and a FORMAT LPRINT "U"and having successfully converted the SAVE and LOAD commands to +3 syntax.

The difficulty comes when I try to send anything to the printer, having set the latter online and with dipswitch 2-1 OFF as instructed.The program then says the printer is online, and stops with "Nonsense in BASIC", appar- ently caused by the POKE @VAL"6" command which occurs several times in the program and per- plexes me as much as it does the +3 editor - I think it's the "@" which causes the problem.

The editorial in Outlet Extra 1 refers to a special +3 version of UNITRANS+. But it would seem that what I have on my 3" disc is the microdrive version. If I select the "manual" option,I get a message at the foot of the

screen like SAVE * "m";1;"name" LINE 1 which the +3 editor won't accept. If I then delete the * "m";1; and hit ENTER, I get a system reset.

I enclose a sample printout made with OUTPRINT. The problems speak for themselves.

Let me conclude with some +3 conundrums...

1.Is it possible to do a NEW without being thrown back to the LOADER menu?

2.When "disk" is loaded directly from the LOADER menu and during RUNning gives rise to an error message, any keypress causes the

LOADER menu to reappear and if ENTER is accidently touched, the program reloads from scratch. Is there any way of gaining access to the BASIC editor when such an error occurs?

3.Lastly,is it possible to enter SCREEN mode (i.e. the "lower" screen) by means of an instruct- ion within a program line?

Yours sincerely

J.R.CLEVELAND.

To Mr. J.R. Cleveland from Brian

After Charlie Kingwell's letter in OUTLET 31 describing how he paged through OUTLET on his back and now your "cumfy armchair" idea I'm getting the impression our readership is so laid back it's a wonder they switch on. So we begin next month with cursor control in text mode. Future issues may use speech control but someone may suffer a sore throat so work has begun on an alpha-wave detector that will respond to thought. Ultimately, each issue will come with a lovely assistant who will turn the pages for you!

Seriously, joysticks are out as there are different standards. Kempston crashes those without it so a special routine would be needed to detect it.The Sinclair type uses the equivalent of some number keys which are already in use for pageing. Can anyone with a Sinclair joystick confirm this?

I can't help with CP/M but could the HURRYDUMP (OUTLET 9) code be used to dump text off-screen? If a normal +3 code file can be loaded or the file converted to CP/M format and loaded then it may work. I would expect there's a public domain screen dump.Does anyone know?

I see two possible approaches to the +3 printer bug. One is to disassemble the routine at 23354 to see exactly what it does with the two POKEs and if it may be achieved with some separate code that doesn't need the program to STOP. Another is to use an "ON ERROR GO TO" piece of code that will jump to another line of BASIC if a STOP occurs. It seems to me that in either case, the code and/or POKEs might be ideally placed in something like CATLOADER so you would just need to load whatever program you want to use with CATLOADER and it would be ready to print. I've made a note to have a look at the problem unless someone else beats me to it...

The "POKE @ 6"'s in LC10 DRAW are Disciple/+D printer commands and should be replaced thus...

POKE @ 6,1

```text
           ----------
```

+3        FORMAT LPRINT "U"

OPUS OR M/DRIVE     OPEN #3;"B" OR SAM

KEMPSTON E   COPY :REM CHR$ 0 (may need separate line called by a GO SUB)

For POKE @6,0 replace above with "E" for +3,"T" for Opus/M/drive, "P" for SAM and CHR$ 1 for the Kempston E.

I tried again to get UNITRANS + to work on a +3. I thought I managed to get a quick test operating once although it was important to be in"two-lines-at- the-bottom-of-the- screen-edit- mode" (there must be a better name for it!). However, after spending hours converting the whole thing so the syntax was correct I found, like you, that it reset at the end. I'm almost sure it did work once so I may look at the problem again with a fresh mind another day.

Mike Haine has re-written the OUTPRINT code and it will appear each month as an option in text mode under the name "TABLOID" starting next month.

It should be possible to write some code to achieve NEW without returning to the loader menu but it would be more effort to load the code than to return from the menu.

I don't think there is any easy way but would be delighted if anyone knows differently as it annoys me too!

You can SAVE a totally empty BASIC program,that is,with NO LINES AT ALL using SAVE"X".Then, in normal programs, instead of NEW, use LOAD"X" to clear out BASIC.

The "feature" that re-loads "DISK" if you press ENTER after an error can be avoided in two ways...

Firstly, DON'T PRESS ENTER! I tend to press the down cursor to cause the loader menu to show and then again to select +3 BASIC and then ENTER.

The other way is to MERGE any OUTLET"DISK" loader file, delete all lines except 1001 and reSAVE it. Then MERGE it in your own programs or in a "DISK" loader such as CATLOADER.You need a GO SUB 1001 in the program.However, Brian Gaff tells me this seems to crash on later versions of the +3 and +2A so try it first.

I have been trying to solve your final query to switch to lower- screen mode from within a program to use in the +3 version of UNITRANS+ but failed. Instead of switching "screen" in the loader menu you can press EXTEND MODE then SYMBOL + 8 together (another Brian Gaff tip!). This works both ways. I reasoned that SHIFTED-EXTENDED MODE 8 is POINT on the original Spectrum (try it in INPUT A$) and the code for POINT is 169 so I had hoped if I could enter 169 then 13 (ENTER) into the ROM editor routine it would switch "screen". However, it didn't work although I did discover methods of calling BASIC commands from machine code which may form the basis of a future OUTLET utility!   -Brian

From John White,  LEICESTER

Dear Ron & Brian,

The enclosed disc carries my CHARMASTER(OUTLET 23)User Guide. [to appear in a future issue-BC] It occurs to me you may like to avoid enquiries from puzzled readers by publishing the miss- ing Basic line:-

720 GOTO VAL "500"

In one of your replies in OUTLET 31 you mentioned your keyboard had its cursor keys at the top right. This reminded me you have a Fuller keyboard. So have I; "Fuller, The FDS Keyboard". I remember once mentioning that I

had problems with the Cursor and Delete keys; sometimes there is no automatic CapsShift,resulting in streams of 5's, 6's, 7's, 8's or 0's which can spoil Tasword! Have you ever had this?Strangely full stop and comma never fail.

- John H B White

Yes indeed!The same thing occurs with the +3 and (presumably) any Spectrum with added cursor keys. I heard that Amstrad made great efforts to solve it but had to accept it in the end. Of course, we have fun with a key no other Spectrum has (I think!) - the SHIFTED-EXTENDED KEY! This has too long a delay built in for me so I frequently get CAT ! rather than CAT 1.         - Brian

From David Wornham, WORCS. I am progressing well with the SAM conversion of FLEXIPAGE, hence the inclusion in OUTBOARD. Any order received before it's ready will receive a letter and the cheque will not be paid in before dispatch.

I seem to have better luck than you with MGT's service. I received their updated DOS disk on 16th March which includes a couple of machine code "fixers". This overcomes the SAVE problem in MODE 1 but has yet to overcome the problem of a SAVE LINE command within a program which SAVEs O.K. but stops with an error message and the SAVE DATA A$() with a program which

saves the PROGRAM AND DATA whilst the direct command saves correctly. However, MGT do say the disk is a temporary measure pending a replacement ROM.

MGT state,correctly,the external drive/printer interface needs the disk jumper REMOVED if two internal drives are fitted.Their new instructions include this. They also state the DUMP command is NOT IMPLEMENTED owing to lack of space in the ROM. Although they say use FLASH,I have yet to get this to DUMP and it cannot be included with FLEXIPAGE so I shall write and urge them to include it in the ROM update. In the meantime, a SAM DUMP routine would be a useful item in OUTLET - please.       - David Wornham

To David Wornham from Brian

Thanks David. After receiving your letter I decided to convert our own high-res dump but I have STILL not received the technical manual I ordered from MGT so cannot do any further work on that for the time being.

I then sat down to attempt to develop some BASIC screen dumps and came up with TEEDEE & GEEDEE in this month's issue(SAM ONLY). Both are BASIC procedures with high line numbers which can easily be MERGEd in a program with MERGE "TD" or "GD" and both TD and GD are PD!! i.e. FREEWARE so can be used in your programs.

The bad news is GD, the graphics dump, is very slow and in modes 3 or 4 assumes palette colours 0 to 2 and 8 to 11 will be dark and prints them as black and all other colours come out white so some screens do not print-out perfectly. It is really intended to be a temporary stopgap but does include a nice method of reducing streaking.

TD, the text dump is fast and useful but uses the SCREEN$(X,Y) function which seems to fail in Mode 3 intermittently.

In FLASH,"DRAFT"and"FINAL"do not work at all and probably try to use the non-working ROM routine. The other dump options are o.k. - Brian

From Hugh McGregor, PERTHSHIRE

Dear Each,

THANK YOU VERY MUCH INDEED! I am abso-B*%#Y-lutely over the Moon! That Crossword Puzzle program [PROCROSS in OUTLET 31] is a BELTER!As you will probably have guessed I am just a wee bit pleased with what you accompl- ished.I KNEW it would be special but it's so special that even I (and I am not noted for being easily pleased )am totally dumb- struck!

CONGRATULATIONS!CONGRATULATIONS! CONGRATULATIONS!CONGRATULATIONS! AND YET AGAIN - CONGRATULATIONS!

I have tried all the options and I am, to say the least, highly delighted. You have made an old compiler VERY HAPPY. (and they can't touch you for it you know)

I have been following,with great interest, the continuing saga of the SAM COUPE. Putting all the comments together it seems to me that, like the Curate's egg, it is good in parts. Weighing up all the pro's and con's, I think I will wait until the good bits vastly outweigh the bad. I have no sense of adventure I'm afraid eespecially when adventure could be foolhardy, and will be most likely expensive.

I never cease to be amazed and delighted by your cover pictures. The quality of the artwork and imaginative use of FLASH, BRIGHT etc. and the clever incorporation of movement make them collectors' items I am sure. Sincerely,

Hugh McGregor

Many thanks, Hugh. Glad you like PROCROSS and look out for the front page of July's OUTLET.It's one of the best Spectrum screens I've seen.

**От Francis Davies, DORSET**

    +3        FORMAT LPRINT "U"

  M/DRIVE     OPEN #3;"B"
  ИЛИ SAM

              отдельная строка, вызываемая
              через GO SUB)

Вы можете сохранить абсолютно пустую программу на BASIC, то есть ВООБЩЕ БЕЗ СТРОК, с помощью команды SAVE "X". Затем в обычных программах вместо NEW используйте LOAD "X", чтобы очистить память BASIC.

Эту «особенность» с перезагрузкой файла «DISK», если после ошибки нажать ENTER, можно обойти двумя путями...

Другой способ — объединить (MERGE) любой файл загрузчика «DISK» из OUTLET, удалить все строки, кроме 1001, и пересохранить его. Затем делайте MERGE этой строки в свои программы или в загрузчик «DISK», такой как CATLOADER. В программе вам понадобится GO SUB 1001. Впрочем, Brian Gaff говорит мне, что на более поздних версиях +3 и +2A это, похоже, вызывает сбой, так что сначала проверьте.

Однако это не сработало, хотя я открыл для себя способы вызова команд BASIC из машинного кода, что может лечь в основу будущей утилиты для OUTLET!
